sources.title: Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors (RIN 0694-AK50), Interim final rule
key_facts: ACTION: Interim final rule.

First, this rule establishes new restrictions which will apply for exports, reexports, or transfers (in-country) to overseas data centers that remotely supply significant volumes of compute to companies headquartered in Country Group D:5 or Macau.

a license will be required to export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) advanced semiconductors to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, or Brazil ... – countries which present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion.

The license requirement for these five countries will not apply to semiconductors destined to companies headquartered in, or whose ultimate parent company is headquartered in, the United States, provided certain reporting requirements are met.

Commerce will be actively monitoring for countries that tolerate evasion of this IFR and will consider a range of consequences for such countries, such as import restrictions, new license requirements on advanced semiconductor exports, downgrading the country's status in the U.S. export control regime, and Entity List designations and temporary export prohibitions
Finally, the IFR formally rescinds the regulations implementing the Biden-era AI Diffusion Rule. The AI Diffusion Rule has never been enforced.
DATES: This rule is effective [INSERT DATE OF PUBLICATION IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER].
Comments on the revisions and additions in this rule must be received by BIS no later than [INSERT DATE 60 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER].

You may not knowingly export, reexport, or transfer (in-county) items specified in paragraph (a) of § 744.24 for use in a data center to or within any destination worldwide that will provide access to more than 12,000,000 "aggregate TPP" (either at one data center or through 'linked data centers'

Any data center providing significant volume of compute power to companies headquartered, or with an ultimate parent headquartered, in Macau or Country Group D:5 prior to the publication date of this rule that wishes to continue providing these services must obtain a license with 90 days of the effective date of this IFR or face future export restrictions.

the license requirement will not apply to 'commercial recommender systems,' such as those used by online retailers and social media companies, as these functions do not pose the same national security threat.
(c) License review policy. Applications for licenses required by this section will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis.

There is a case-by-case license review policy for license applications for exports of commodities with a TPP ... less than 21,000, and a 'total DRAM bandwidth' ... less than 6,500 GB/s, when destined to end-users located in China or Macau

Data centers, foreign foundries, and chip exporters are required to perform robust due diligence on their customers, including any direct or indirect ownership or control by persons in Country Group D:5 or Macau
